```{r,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE}
#| echo: false
library(tidyverse)

tweets <- read_csv("data/tweets.csv")
```

## The Data
This data was taken from the Barack Obama Presidential Library created by the National Archives. The data set contains information about every tweet and retweet made by Obama through the @POTUS44 Twitter handle. 

You can access the data for yourself here: [National Archives - Obama Tweets](https://www.obamalibrary.gov/digital-research-room/archived-white-house-websites-and-social-media)

```{r}
glimpse(tweets)
```

```{r}
##Data Cleaning 
tweets2 <- tweets |> 
    mutate(
        timestamp = ymd_hms(timestamp),
        text_lower = str_to_lower(text),
        text = str_replace_all(text, "&amp;", "&")
    )
```

## Text Analysis

### Tweet Length
```{r}
tweets1 <- tweets2 |> 
    filter(!is.na(text)) |> 
    filter(is.na(retweeted_status_id), !str_detect(text, "^RT @")) |> 
    mutate(length = str_length(text_lower)) |> 
    mutate(mean = mean(length)) |> 
    mutate(length_ratio = length/mean) |> 
    select(length_ratio, length, tweet_id, timestamp, text, source) |> 
    arrange(desc(length))

tweets1 |> 
    summarize(mean = mean(length), max = max(length), min = min(length))

print(tweets1)
```

Obama's tweets averaged 126 characters. The longest post had 171 characters, and the shortest tweet contained only 17 characters. The second table displays the length of each post in descending order. Further, it takes the relative length of each post to the mean.  

```{r}
tweets1 |> 
    ggplot(aes(x=timestamp, y=length)) + 
    geom_point(alpha = 0.15,size=0.8, color = "#1DA1F2") +
    labs(title = "Length of Obama's Tweets Over Time", 
            x = "Date Posted", y = "Tweet Length (characters)") +
    theme_minimal()
```

Obama's tweets averaged around 130 characters from 2009 to 2011. From 2011 to 2016, the tweets averaged at around 140 characters---the character limit of tweets at the time. However, toward the end of 2016, we see a jump in character count to a new level. This could be due to Twitter changing what counts toward the 140 character limit in September of 2016. This change meant that media attachments and quoted elements no longer counted towards the limit, allowing the total characters to go above 140.

### Most common Hashtags
```{r}
tweets2 |> 
    filter(is.na(retweeted_status_id), !str_detect(text, "^RT @")) |> 
    mutate(hashtag = str_extract_all(text_lower, "#\\w+")) |> 
    unnest(hashtag) |> 
    filter(!is.na(hashtag)) |> 
    group_by(hashtag) |> 
    summarize(n=n()) |> 
    arrange(desc(n)) |> 
    slice_head(n=10) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x=n, y = fct_reorder(hashtag,n))) +
        geom_col(fill = "#1DA1F2") +
        labs(title = "Top 10 Most Used Hashtags", x = NULL, y = "Hashtag")
```

This chart shows the 10 most highly used hashtags by former President Obama in his own tweets. From this data, we can see some of the issues he cared greatly about, including climate action, healthcare, and equal opportunity. 

```{r}
tweets2 |> 
    filter(str_detect(text_lower,"#actonclimate\\b")) |> 
    mutate(month = floor_date(timestamp, "month")) |> 
    group_by(month) |> 
    summarize(n=n()) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x=month, y = n)) +
        geom_line(color = "#1DA1F2") +
        labs(title = "Uses of #ActOnClimate Overtime", x = "Year", y = "Number of Uses")
```

This graph plots the usage of #ActOnClimate overtime in both Obama's own tweets and his retweets. The hashtag was introduced in the middle of 2013 and peaked in usage towards the middle of 2014. It was used constantly in 2015 and dropped in usage towards the end of his second term.

### Most Mentioned 
```{r}
tweets2 |> 
    filter(is.na(retweeted_status_id), !str_detect(text, "^RT @")) |> 
    mutate(mention = str_extract_all(text_lower, "(?<=@)\\w+")) |> 
    unnest(mention) |> 
    filter(!is.na(mention)) |> 
    group_by(mention) |> 
    summarize(n=n()) |> 
    arrange(desc(n)) |> 
    slice_head(n=10) 
```

This table shows the top 10 most mentioned accounts by Barack Obama. @POTUS is the most used mention at 3643 uses because many of the tweets quote the president and end with a "-@POTUS." Another use of the POTUS mention is when tweeting about events the former president was speaking at, including uses like "at 6:50am ET, @POTUS speaks...". The next most used menion is @VP, @whitehouse, and @FLOTUS.

### Tweets Overtime
```{r}
tweets2 |> 
    mutate(year = year(timestamp)) |> 
    group_by(year) |> 
    summarize(n = n()) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = year, y = n)) +
        geom_line(color = "#1DA1F2") +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2009:2016) +
        labs(title = "Obama's Tweets Over the Years", x = "Year", y = "Number of Tweets")
```

This graph shows Obama's tweets over his years in office. It shows that his Twitter handle was used more in his second term from 2013-2017, and was used most in 2014 and 2015. This surge in usage in 2014 could be due to his decleration of the year as a "year of action," in which he enacted many executive orders and policy initiatives to address many issues of the time.

### State of the Union
Days sorted by volume of tweets
```{r}
tweets2 |> 
    mutate(date = as_date(timestamp)) |> 
    group_by(date) |> 
    summarize(n = n()) |> 
    arrange(desc(n))
```

Hashtags by usage on Jan. 29, 2014
```{r}
tweets2 |> 
  mutate(date = as_date(timestamp)) |> 
  filter(date == ymd("2014-01-29")) |> 
  mutate(hashtag = str_extract_all(text_lower, "(?<=#)\\w+")) |> 
  unnest(hashtag) |> 
  group_by(hashtag) |> 
  summarize(n = n()) |> 
  arrange(desc(n))
```

Original tweets and retweets on Jan. 29, 2014
```{r}
tweets2 |> 
    mutate(date = as_date(timestamp)) |> 
    filter(date == ymd("2014-01-29")) |> 
    mutate(retweet = !is.na(retweeted_status_id) | str_detect(text, "^RT @")) |> 
    mutate(retweet = fct_recode(factor(retweet), "Retweet" = "TRUE", "Original" = "FALSE")) |> 
    group_by(retweet) |> 
    summarize(n=n()) 
```

January 28, 2014 was former President Obama's State of the Union Address. The following day, Jan. 29, was the day with the highest number of tweets and retweets through Obama's Twitter account. His tweets reflect this, as almost 50 of the tweets include #SOTU. On that day, he wrote 170 original tweets, and 20 were retweets.
